title: Crete or Rhodes: which Greek island suits your holiday?
author: Matt
intro: Pick Rhodes for an easy week with a medieval old town and beaches close together, and Crete for a longer trip with a car, gorges, Minoan palaces and more variety. Here's how they compare.
seo_title: Crete or Rhodes? Rhodes for a week, Crete for longer
seo_description: Rhodes suits an easy week: one base, a medieval old town, beaches close by. Crete is six times bigger, best for 10-14 days with a car. Full comparison.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **One week, one base:** Rhodes
- **10 days or more:** Crete
- **Hottest in summer:** Rhodes, about 31°C
- **Best for hiking:** Crete

Both are about four hours' flight from the UK, both use the euro, and both are two hours ahead. The difference is size. Crete is roughly six times bigger than Rhodes, and that changes everything about how you plan the trip.

sections.heading: Crete and Rhodes side by side
sections.text:
| | Crete | Rhodes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Size | about 260 km end to end | about 80 km end to end |
| Airports | Heraklion and Chania | Rhodes |
| Ideal stay | 10 to 14 nights | 7 to 10 nights |
| Car needed? | Yes, really | Helpful, not essential |
| July high | about 29°C | about 31°C |
| Big sights | Knossos, Samaria Gorge, Chania | Rhodes Old Town, Lindos |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Crete](/destinations/crete) and [Rhodes](/destinations/rhodes) guides.

sections.heading: Why Rhodes works for a week
sections.text:
Rhodes packs a lot into a small island:

- **Rhodes Old Town** is one of the best-preserved medieval towns in Europe and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with the Knights' Street and the Palace of the Grand Master inside its walls.
- **Lindos**, an hour or so down the east coast, is a whitewashed village under a clifftop acropolis, with a beach right below.
- **Prasonisi**, in the far south, is where two seas meet at a sandy spit, popular with windsurfers.
- **Anthony Quinn Bay** is a small, clear cove for snorkelling.

Because distances are short, you can stay in one place and still see all of this on day trips, by bus, taxi or a few days' car hire. There's also a ferry to the pastel harbour town of **Symi** for a day out.

Local knowledge: Rhodes is one of the sunniest Greek islands, and its beach season runs a little later into October than many others.

sections.heading: Why Crete needs more time
sections.text:
Crete is the biggest Greek island, and driving from Chania in the west to Heraklion in the middle takes about two hours. Most people pick one end and explore from there, or split the trip between two bases.

- **West Crete:** Chania's Venetian harbour, the pink-tinged sand at Elafonissi and the Balos lagoon, reached by boat or a rough track.
- **Central Crete:** the Minoan palace of **Knossos**, linked to the legend of the Minotaur, and the archaeological museum in Heraklion.
- **The south coast:** quieter villages and beaches, reached over the mountains.

The **Samaria Gorge** is one of Europe's best-known walks, about 16 km downhill to the sea. It's usually open from May to October, weather permitting, though in 2026 it opened late, on 19 May, after storm damage to the trail.

Watch out: Crete's roads are long and winding, and many beaches are well away from the resorts. Without a car, you'll see a fraction of the island.

sections.heading: Beaches
sections.text:
Both islands have very good beaches, but they're different:

- **Rhodes:** long, sheltered beaches and calm water on the east coast, from Faliraki down to Lindos, which suits a classic beach week. The west coast is windier.
- **Crete:** more variety, from the shallow lagoons at Balos and Elafonissi to quiet coves on the south coast. The best ones often need a drive and an early start to beat the coach trips in July and August.

sections.heading: Costs and tickets
sections.text:
Prices are similar on both islands, and both have plenty of all-inclusive and self-catering options. The costs to plan for:

- **Car hire** in Crete, for most of your stay.
- **Knossos:** about €20 for adults in 2026.
- **Samaria Gorge:** €10 in 2025.

Check the official Greek heritage ticket site, hhticket.gr, for current prices and to book ahead in summer.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text:
The best months for both are **May, June, September and October**, when the sea is warm but it's not too hot for sightseeing. July and August are hot and busy, cooled a little by the meltemi wind.

Direct flights from the UK run mainly from April or May to October. Out of season, Rhodes Town and Heraklion stay open, but most resorts close, so neither is a winter-sun choice.

sections.heading: So, which one?
sections.text:
- **Choose Rhodes** for a week with one base, history on your doorstep, easy beaches and the least driving.
- **Choose Crete** for 10 to 14 days, a road trip, hiking and the feeling of a place with more to discover.

If you've already done one, the other makes a very different second trip. Our guide on [how to choose between two holidays](/blog/how-to-choose-between-two-holidays) can help, or browse more islands on our [holidays in Greece](/destinations/holidays-in-greece) page, such as [Corfu](/destinations/corfu) or [Kos](/destinations/kos). Can't agree? Add both to somewhere.party and let the draw pick, or read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday).

faqs.question: Is Crete or Rhodes better for a first trip to Greece?
faqs.answer: Rhodes is easier for a first trip, with short distances and one base. Crete rewards a longer stay with a car.

faqs.question: Do you need a car in Crete?
faqs.answer: For most trips, yes. Crete is about 260 km long, and many of the best beaches and sights are a long way from the resorts.

faqs.question: Is Rhodes hotter than Crete?
faqs.answer: Slightly. Rhodes averages about 31°C in July and August, against about 29°C in Crete.

faqs.question: How long should you spend in Crete?
faqs.answer: At least 10 nights to see more than one area. A week works if you stay in one region, such as Chania and the west.
